hypothesis: SPY 20/50-day SMA crossover with volume confirmation outperforms buy-and-hold on a 5-year window.
rejection_reason: failed walk-forward robustness (only 2 of 4 out-of-sample splits had positive Sharpe); looked good only in-sample.
notes: Full-period Sharpe was attractive but walk-forward exposed regime-dependence around 2022 rate-hike period. Consider revisiting with a volatility-regime filter rather than dropping the idea entirely.

hypothesis: QQQ mean-reverts after closing below its 20-day lower Bollinger Band, but only in low-volatility regimes (current 20d realized vol <= trailing 1yr median); high-vol regimes are explicitly excluded because the prior SMA-crossover strategy (2026-09-01-001) failed walk-forward specifically due to regime-dependence around the 2022 rate-hike period.
rejection_reason: Sharpe ratio -0.30 vs required >= 1.0, a clear (non-borderline) fail on full-sample data (2019-2026, QQQ). Only 14 trades / 81 days in market over 7.7 years; strategy lost money on a risk-adjusted basis. Remaining validators (transaction costs, walk-forward, parameter sensitivity) skipped per RESEARCH_LOOP.md Step 5/6: a negative full-sample Sharpe cannot pass a stricter out-of-sample check, so running them would not change the outcome.
notes: Novelty: distinct from 2026-09-01-001 (SPY SMA crossover, trend-following, rejected on walk-forward) and 2026-09-02-001 (BTC funding-rate mean reversion, rejected on data feasibility) -- this is a QQQ mean-reversion idea with an explicit vol-regime filter designed to avoid exactly the regime-dependence that broke 2026-09-01-001. Vol-regime filter worked as intended (kept MDD to 15%, low market exposure), but the underlying entry signal itself has no discernible edge on QQQ daily bars. Two ideas for a future loop, recorded in the backtest report: (1) try a coarser Bollinger band (2.5-3 std) / shorter timeframe to get a stronger per-trade edge with fewer, higher-conviction trades; (2) the full-sample annualized Sharpe metric may unfairly penalize any low-market-exposure strategy during QQQ's 2019-2026 secular uptrend -- a days-in-market-only comparison could be a fairer validator refinement. Also fixed two real scaffold bugs this loop: vectorbt import was broken by plotly>=5.24 removing scattermapbox (pinned plotly<5.24 in requirements.txt), and validators.py check_sharpe_ratio/check_max_drawdown crashed with "Index frequency is None" (fixed by passing freq="D" explicitly to the vectorbt returns accessor).

hypothesis: BTC/USDT exhibits positive absolute (time-series) momentum: long when trailing 90-day return is positive, flat otherwise, driven by momentum-chasing retail flow and slow information diffusion in crypto markets.
rejection_reason: Max drawdown 66.0% vs budget (25-35%), and Sharpe 0.92 narrowly missed threshold of 1.0 at the pre-registered 90-day lookback. Parameter sensitivity and transaction-cost-survival both passed, but the hard risk gate (max drawdown) failed decisively -- the momentum filter did not meaningfully reduce drawdown relative to buy-and-hold BTC.
notes: Novelty: distinct from 2026-09-01-001 (SPY dual-SMA crossover, equity, failed walk-forward) -- same trend-following family but different asset class and signal construction (single trailing-return threshold vs MA crossover); distinct from 2026-09-02-001 (BTC funding-rate mean reversion, rejected on data feasibility) -- this only needs OHLCV; distinct from 2026-09-03-001 (QQQ Bollinger mean-reversion, rejected on Sharpe) -- trend-following not mean-reversion, crypto not equity. Found a scaffold bug: validation/validators.py::check_walk_forward calls vbt.utils.splitting.RangeSplitter which does not exist in the installed vectorbt version (AttributeError) -- walk-forward was skipped for this reason (not fixed this loop since MDD failure was already decisive). Parameter sweep (lookback 30/60/90/120/150d) showed shorter lookbacks (30-60d) clear Sharpe>=1.0, worth revisiting with per-lookback MDD check and a vol-targeting/position-sizing overlay to attack the drawdown problem specifically, rather than abandoning momentum on BTC entirely.
